title: Electronics Fundamentals Module 1: Lab Safety, ESD & Multimeter Setup
overview: Covers electrical shock thresholds, Electrostatic Discharge (ESD) protection, and proper Digital Multimeter (DMM) lead placement.

1.label: ESD (Electrostatic Discharge) Protection
1.what: Prevents invisible static electricity from your body (as low as 30V–100V) from frying sensitive CMOS/MOSFET chips.
1.exam_facts: You can't feel static until ~3,000V, but microchips die at <100V. Wrist straps contain a built-in 1 Megaohm (1MΩ) safety resistor to limit current if you touch live power.
1.troubleshoot: Always clip your wrist strap to the grounded ESD mat or bench ground *before* picking up an IC, RAM stick, or circuit board.

2.label: DMM Jacks & Internal Fuses
2.what: The three/four input ports on a multimeter: COM (Common/Black), V/Ω/mA (Red for voltage, resistance, small current), and 10A (Red for high current).
2.exam_facts: 100mA (0.1A) across the heart can be lethal. Never measure resistance (Ω) or continuity on a powered circuit—it will give false readings or damage the meter.
2.troubleshoot: If your DMM reads '0.00' on every current test, you likely blew the internal ceramic fuse by accidentally probing voltage while the red lead was still in the mA/10A jack!

3.label: Measuring Voltage (Parallel Connection)
3.what: Voltage is electrical pressure *difference* between two points, so you touch the probes across a component without breaking the circuit.
3.exam_facts: A voltmeter has extremely high internal resistance (~10MΩ) so it draws almost zero current and doesn't disturb the circuit.
3.troubleshoot: Red probe on positive/high side, Black on Ground (COM). If you get a negative sign (-12.04V), your leads are simply reversed.

4.label: Measuring Current (Series Connection)
4.what: Current is the flow of electrons *through* a wire, so you must physically break the circuit open and insert the meter in line.
4.exam_facts: An ammeter has near-zero internal resistance. Putting it in parallel across a battery creates a direct dead short!
4.troubleshoot: Start with the red lead in the 10A jack first if you don't know how much current the circuit draws, then move down to mA for precision.
